how.heading: How it works

step1.title: Sign in with GC Stats
step1.body: If your GC Stats profile is linked, your tournament history is added automatically. If not, find it in a few clicks.

step2.title: Create your post
step2.body: Role, rank, languages, region, experience, and your agent tierlist. Everything is structured, nothing to write.

step3.title: Get seen everywhere
step3.body: Your post goes live on the site, is sent to subscribed Discord servers and shared on Twitter.

how.freshBody: Posts expire after 10 days. We remind you on day 7, one click to renew.

tierlist.heading: Your agent tierlist, readable at a glance
tierlist.body: No more "I play a bit of everything". Every player ranks their agents on five levels, and teams filter by agent directly.
tierlist.filterHint: Filter example: "can play Viper" means Viper in the top two levels.

verified.heading: Profiles linked to GC Stats
verified.body: Link your post to your GC Stats profile, which tracks Game Changers tournaments, and your background shows up: tournaments played, teams, results. Until our staff approves the link, the post mentions it.
verified.verifiedHint: Link approved, GC Stats history shown.
verified.pendingHint: Link request waiting for staff approval.
verified.noneHint: No tournament yet, the post is shown as usual.

discord.heading: Posts delivered straight to your server
discord.body: Add the bot to your Discord server and choose what you receive. Every new post matching your criteria is sent automatically, with its tierlist and a link to the post.

add.title: Add the bot
add.body: Invite it to your server in one click, it only needs to write in the channels you pick.

channel.title: Pick one or more channels
channel.body: One channel for EU LFT, another for staff: each channel has its own setup.

filters.title: Choose what you receive
filters.body: Post types, regions, roles, rank, languages, agents, experience, availability. The same filters as on the site.

receive.title: Get posts live
receive.body: New and renewed posts are sent as soon as they go live, with no duplicates.

twitter.name: Twitter
twitter.title: Follow us on Twitter
twitter.body: Posts are shared on our account with the tierlist as an image, to reach the whole scene.

cta.title: Ready to scout?
cta.body: Filters saved in your browser, no account needed to browse.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: GC Scouting collects only what it needs to publish posts, let you talk with teams and warn you when your posts expire. Here is what we store, why, and how to delete it.

login.title: Sign in with GC Stats
login.text: You sign in with your GC Stats account: we never see your password. At each sign in, with your consent, GC Stats sends us:
login.identity: Identity: your GC Stats identifier, username and avatar.
login.email: Email: your verified address, used only for expiry reminders if you turn them on.
login.discord: Discord: the identifier of your linked Discord account, for direct message reminders and to identify you when you report a post.
login.player: Player profile: the GC Stats profile linked to your account, to show the verified badge and your tournament history.
login.tokens: GC Stats access tokens are encrypted in our database and only used to act on your behalf with GC Stats (for example a profile link request). They are revoked when you delete your account.
login.created: Account age: the creation date of your GC Stats account, to show the "New account" badge in messages during its first 7 days.
login.sanctions: Sanctions: your active GC Stats sanctions (mute, suspension, ban) and their end date, checked before each message or post to block sending while the sanction lasts. An active warning shows the "Warned" badge in messages.

public.title: What is public
public.text: A post is visible to everyone, without signing in: username, post type, region, country, languages, rank, roles, tier list, experience, availability and presentation.
public.contact: Contact details: the Discord, X account or email you add to a post are shown publicly so teams can reach you. Only add what you are fine making public.
public.gcs: If your profile is linked, the history shown (teams, tournaments, results) comes from GC Stats public data.

relay.title: Sharing on Discord and X
relay.text: Active posts are sent automatically to the Discord channels that set up our bot, and can be shared on our X account with their share image. When a post is closed, deleted or removed, or when you delete your account, our bot also deletes its messages from these channels. An expired post stays there until then. Posts already shared on X stay online, as do copies made by other people.

private.title: Technical data
private.sessions: Sessions: a fingerprint of your session token (never the token itself), the browser used (user agent) and the creation and expiry dates, so you can review and secure your sessions.
private.country: Country: the country of your connection, provided by our hosting network, is only used to preselect your region in the filters. It is never stored.
private.logs: Logs: our host keeps short lived technical logs (errors, requests) for troubleshooting.
private.noTracking: No audience measurement, no ads, no third party trackers and no data resale.

notifications.title: Expiry reminders
notifications.text: Email and Discord direct message reminders are off by default and only sent if you turn them on. They contain links to renew or delete your post without signing in, valid for 14 days. You can turn them off at any time.

delegation.title: Delegated access
delegation.text: If you give someone else access to your profile (agent, manager), we store that link so they can publish and manage posts in your name. You can revoke this access at any time from your account. In the messaging, they write under their own name and the profile they manage is shown next to it.

messages.title: Messages
messages.text: When you write to a member from a post, we store the conversation: both profiles, the post it started from, every message with its date, and the account that actually wrote it if you manage someone else's profile. We also store when you last read it, for unread messages, and the list of members you block.
messages.staff: Conversations are not end to end encrypted: our moderation team can read them to handle a report, review a held message or look into abuse. They can hide a message. Do not share anything sensitive there.
messages.automod: Automatic moderation: each message is sent to the OpenAI moderation API (United States) before delivery, without your username or identifier. OpenAI does not use it to train its models and keeps it for 30 days at most. A message flagged as harmful is held until the team decides.
messages.links: Links: only Discord, X, GC Stats, VLR and Liquipedia links are clickable. Other links are hidden behind a warning, nothing is checked or stored apart from the message.
messages.alerts: Alerts: an email or a Discord direct message tells you about new messages, once per unread streak, without copying their content. They are on by default and can be turned off from the My account page. If you manage someone else's profile, you also get the alerts of its conversations, with your own settings.

moderation.title: Reports and moderation
moderation.text: When you report a post or a message, we store the reason, your message and your account. Moderation happens in a private Discord channel and in an admin area of the website: every action (removal, restore, hidden message, sharing on X) is logged with the account of the team member who did it.
moderation.reporter: Your identity is never shown to the author of the reported post or message. Only our moderation team can see it.

retention.title: Retention
retention.posts: A post expires 10 days after it is published or last renewed. It then leaves the list and the Discord channels, but its link stays available with a banner until you delete it.
retention.sessions: A session lasts 30 days, or until you sign out.
retention.account: Your account and everything attached to it (posts, sent messages, blocks, sessions, delegated access, profile link) are kept until you delete it from the <account>My account</account> page. Reports you filed and the Discord messages of your posts are then deleted too.
retention.messages: Messages are kept as long as the conversation exists. When you delete your account, the messages you sent are deleted. The other member's messages stay in their list.

rights.title: Your rights (GDPR)
rights.text: You have a right of access, rectification, objection and erasure of your data. From the <account>My account</account> page, you can export all your data as JSON or delete your account in one click. Your GC Stats account is never touched.
rights.contact: For any other request: <mail>{email}</mail>. You can also file a complaint with the CNIL (French data protection authority) if you believe your rights are not respected.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.text: We only use technical cookies required for the website to work, so no consent banner is needed.
cookies.profile: sc_profile: the active profile when you manage someone else's profile.
cookies.oauth: sc_oauth: secures the sign in with GC Stats, deleted right after.
cookies.storage: Local storage: your post filters and your timezone, which stay in your browser.

tierListGuide.title: Understanding our tierlist
tierListGuide.intro: Every player post comes with an agent tierlist. Here is why it looks the way it does, and how to fill yours so it actually helps teams.

scene.title: Built with the scene
scene.text: The format was not picked at random: it was designed with experienced players, coaches and managers of the Game Changers scene, people who scout and recruit every split.
scene.why: Their feedback was clear: a long list of agents tells a team nothing. What they need to know is which agents you can play in a match tomorrow, which ones need some work, and which ones you are ready to learn for the team.
scene.credit: The tier list was notably worked on with LittleBigSpy, IGL at ZennIT Orange GC, whose experience of the scene helped define how agents should be ranked.

tiers.title: The three tiers
tiers.confident: Agents you can play in an official match right now, with the lineups, utility and habits that go with them.
tiers.improve: Agents you already know how to play, but that need practice before you are comfortable on them in a match.
tiers.canLearn: Agents you do not play yet, but are willing to pick up if the team needs it.
tiers.aside: Agents left aside are simply not shown on your post. There is no "bad" row: an empty slot says more than a guess.

highlight.title: Highlight the agents you know how to play
highlight.text: The tierlist is there to highlight the agents you know how to play, not to rank every agent of the game or to give your opinion on the meta.
highlight.honest: Be honest: teams will check it during tryouts, and a short accurate tierlist is worth more than a full one.
highlight.notMeta: Rank your own level on each agent, not how strong the agent is in the current patch.
highlight.filter: Your first two rows are used by the "can play" filter, on the site and on Discord: they decide which searches your post shows up in.
highlight.example: Example: a controller and sentinel player, confident on their main pool, with a few initiators to polish.
